newsitem.title: ITALY: Pesticides are damaging developing world crop-FAO.
newsitem.headline: Pesticides are damaging developing world crop-FAO.

text.p: Misuse of pesticides is wrecking land in the developing world and putting the health of poorly-trained farmers at risk, the United Nations Food and Agricultural Organisation (FAO) said on Thursday.

The Rome-based agency called for improved equipment and better training for farmers in Asia and South America, saying they were often completely unaware of application procedures and safety standards.

"In many countries, the only specialists offering advice to farmers on application technology, handling and calibration of their equipment are representatives of pesticide companies," FAO officer Theodor Friedrich said in a statement.
"To improve pesticide application, the introduction of good standard quality equipment and operator training is essential," he said.
The U.N. agency said indiscriminate use of pesticides in Pakistan was polluting groundwater, whereas in India above-average levels of the spray had been found in food crops.

Southeast Asian farmers in Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines did not know how to use pesticides due to poor training which left them in danger of contamination from the spray, the statement said.
In South America, Brazilian and Colombian farmers used excessive volumes of pesticides which contaminated soil and leaked into water tables.
FAO said weekly spraying levels of 6,000 litres per hectare in Colombia and 10,000 per hectare in Brazil could be cut by 90 percent if sufficient technology was implemented.
